Former Coronation Street star Tracy Shaw has shared a tearful update regarding her breast cancer diagnosis, revealing that surgery is currently not an option as her tumours have failed to shrink.

The 52-year-old actress and singer, famed for her role as Maxine Peacock in the long-running ITV soap, first announced her diagnosis in April.

She has since been providing regular updates on social media, detailing her chemotherapy journey and the challenges she faces.

Her latest emotional video, posted on Instagram on Thursday, followed an ultrasound scan, where she conveyed the difficult news that her tumours had not reduced in size, making she will not be able to have surgery at this stage.

The soap star shared a video while leaving hospital, and said: “As I told you all, I had my ultrasounds today to find out if (my) lesions had shrunk.

“I also needed to check a lump that I’d found on the other breast, the right breast.”

Shaw said her “good news” was that the lumps she found “are all cysts”, but revealed the treatment to shrink the lesions on her left breast was not as successful as she had hoped.

“I thought they’d shrunk but basically they’ve gone from being circular to oval, but not really shrunk in size. I don’t know what I was expecting,” the actress said.

She continued: “I think I’m just expecting some results of what I felt. What the body has had to go through to… I don’t know.

“Maybe a few more rounds will be all it takes but I know they can’t operate until they shrink it.

“So I thought I would give you a live update this time. I was just expecting some… miraculous miracle. Maybe it’s to come.”

In the caption, Shaw said: “After hearing the news, went to TK max to buy more hats. Followed with a huge M&S food shop to cheer me up.

“Thank you to you all for your lovely messages.”

The comments were flooded with support from fans and fellow stars, with Waterloo Road actress Kym Marsh saying “so much love to you babe”.

Shaw is best known for her role on Coronation Street, having appeared in the soap from 1995 to 2003 before being murdered by infamous serial killer Richard Hillman (Brian Capron).

She has also appeared in other TV shows such as The Blue Room and Mile High, and embarked on a brief singing career in the late 1990s.

A celebrity plastic surgeon, dubbed “The Boob God,” is facing four medical malpractice lawsuits.

Dr. Leonard “Lenny” Hochstein, a plastic surgeon in Miami, Florida, and ex-husband of Real Housewives of Miami star Lisa Hochstein, was slapped with a trio of lawsuits this month, in addition to a fourth filed in June 2025.

The lawsuits, all filed in Miami-Dade County, paint a similar picture of multiple clients who came to Hochstein for cosmetic breast augmentations and lifts and left unsatisfied with their results due to mistakes allegedly made by the surgeon.

The surgeon, whose office phone greeting refers to him as a “World Renowned Celebrity Plastic Surgeon,” is accused of leaving some patients with lasting pain among other injuries that include scarring and deformities, the lawsuits claim.

“These are allegations, not facts,” Hochstein told the Miami Herald over text. “I am fully prepared to defend myself and expect to prevail in all three cases.” The Independent has contacted Hochstein for further comment.

open image in gallery Miami plastic surgeon Dr. Leonard Hochstein with his ex-wife, reality TV star Lisa Hochstein. Dr. Hochstein is facing four separate medical malpractice lawsuits related to botched boob jobs ( Getty )

On Hochstein’s website, it says he has performed “over 30,000 breast augmentations, revisions, lifts and reductions throughout his career. The wealth of experience he has accumulated and the dedication to his craft have led Dr. Hochstein to be recognized as the top plastic surgeon in the country and called the ‘Boob God™’ in the world of plastic surgery.”

One former patient, Miriam Pavlovsky, said that after her May 2025 breast augmentation and breast lift with silicone implants, she “continues to suffer from permanent anatomical distortion, pain and the likelihood of future corrective surgeries.”

Another patient, Alana Jaffery, claimed in her lawsuit that her primary care physician cleared her for surgery in May 2025 despite other medical issues like obesity, prediabetes, iron deficiency anemia and high blood pressure “on the understanding that these factors would be accounted for.”

Jaffery faced multiple post-surgery complications and, according to the lawsuit, “endured months of painful and invasive wound management, including repeated surgical debridement, treatment of bacterial infection, prolonged packing and dressing care and wound-vac therapy.”

“She continues to suffer permanent abdominal scarring contour deformity and the likelihood of future reconstructive procedures,” the lawsuit adds.

Pauline Pearlman saw Hochstein for a consultation for a cosmetic breast surgery, and a handwritten consultation note from Hochstein showed they were considering an augmentation or a breast lift — but not both surgeries. However, in her lawsuit, Pearlman claims Hochstein did them as a combined procedure in March 2022.

“No clinical rationale or therapeutic justification for changing the surgical plan from a single-procedure operation to a combined augmentation-mastoplexy (lift) was documented in the medical records,” according to the lawsuit.

After that operation, a revision and breast lift a year later, Pearlman was left with “persistent breast deformity, including symmastia and right implant malposition, chronic pain, and the need for additional corrective surgery,” the lawsuit claims.

Symmastia is a breast condition, often referred to as “uniboob” or “monoboob,” where the breasts fuse in the center of the chest.

Meanwhile, Tanya Draskovic, whose lawsuit was filed last year, claims that in October 2022 Hochstein recommended a breast lift, implant exchange and removal of scar tissue around the implant.

The procedures, which happened all at once, raised the risk of something going wrong — which the lawsuit claims Hochstein failed to warn Draskovic about beforehand. The lawsuit claims that, in addition to failing to botching the procedures, Hochstein failed to “recognize and treat postoperative complications.”

open image in gallery Hochstein (right) is nicknamed ‘The Boob God’ and was previously married to reality TV star Lisa Hochstein (center) ( Getty )

His failure to treat her complications in a timely manner allegely resulted in Draskovic suffering complications including left breast capsular contracture and deformity, requiring additional surgery, scarring, pain, and left shoulder adhesive capsulitis and bursitis, according to the suit.

A response for Hochstein, filed by his lawyer Brian Engel, denies all of the allegations in the complaint. No response from his attorney has been filed in the other three cases.

Hochstein made headlines earlier this year in April when his ex-wife, Lisa Hochstein, turned herself in to authorities after allegedly spying on the plastic surgeon.

Lisa Hochstein and her ex-boyfriend Jody Glidden had each been charged with one felony count of unlawfully intercepting oral statements made by Dr Hochstein. Glidden was arrested and released on $5,000 bond.

Lisa Hochstein denied all allegations against her and her attorney Jayne Weintraub previously toldThe Independent: “This matter is part of a contentious divorce proceeding and does not belong in criminal court. This morning she voluntarily turned herself in to be processed and will be released on her own recognizance.”

The couple’s marriage was documented on the Bravo series, where Lisa starred in season two of the Miami Housewives. Filming of the series was paused earlier this year due to low viewership.

Lisa and Leonard Hochstein were married for 13 years and have two children. They announced their split in 2022 and finalized their divorce two years later.

Britain's armed forces are ready to protect the country from any attack from Iranian missiles, the government said on Thursday.

It follows a warning from Iran's Revolutionary Guards over the UK allowing US bombers to fly from its bases.

"Our Armed Forces are ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it's on our soil or from abroad. The UK stands ready 24/7 to defend itself," a government spokesperson said.

"This includes through operating a layered approach to air and missile defence, provided by Royal Navy, British Army and Royal Air Force assets equipped with a range of advanced capabilities, working closely with our NATO allies," they added.

Tehran warned on Thursday that RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire is a “legitimate target” for strikes after the US Air Force used it to launch a bombing raid.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) singled out the “British monarchy” as “the main cause of the misfortunes of the people of our region”.

In response to Iran's warning, the spokesperson said Britain's approach remained unchanged and that it was committed to defending its people, interests and allies in accordance with international law while avoiding being drawn into a wider conflict.

Military equipment targeted at an unknown location, during what U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) says are strikes on Iran, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on July 20, 2026 ( U.S. Central Command )

In March, Iran launched two ballistic mis­siles towards the joint UK-US military base on Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, with one missile failing and the other intercepted by a US warship.

An Iranian Shahed one-way attack drone hit also RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus in March, with two other missiles intercepted.

The Ministry of Defence claims it has made “air and missile defence a priority” in the new defence investment plan and has dedicated £790m towards this goal.

Iran's warning came after new prime minister Andy Burnham was notified last week of Britain re-committing to an existing agreement allowing the US to use British bases in what it described as the collective self-defence of the region.

The UK government said on Wednesday that the arrangement covered US defensive operations to degrade missile sites and capabilities used in attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

It signalled a fresh start in the transatlantic partnership after relations with Sir Keir Starmer grew increasingly fractious over the Iran war.

The UK withdrew remaining diplomatic staff from Iran as the conflict with the US continued to escalate with a 12th night of airstrikes.

A statement on the Foreign Office (FCDO) website said: “Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran.

“Our embassy continues to operate remotely.”

The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran, saying British and dual British-Iranian residents face “significant risk of arrest, questioning or detention”.

A similar move was made in February ahead of the start of US and Israeli combat operations.

US Central Command said late on Wednesday that the 12th night of attacks was designed to “further degrade Iran’s ability to threaten civilian mariners and commercial vessels transiting regional waters”.

Announcing the end of the latest wave of strikes on Thursday morning, they said US forces struck military targets including maritime capabilities, missile and drone storage facilities, coastal surveillance sites and air defence assets.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Tottenham set to go head to head for £51m-rated World Cup star, 21, who faced England
Sports.content:
ARSENAL and Tottenham are preparing to go head-to-head in a fierce transfer battle for RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa.

The Norwegian international, 21, has emerged as one of the most sought-after young attackers in Europe after a stellar spell in the Bundesliga.



Nusa shone at the World Cup, featuring six times and scoring Norway’s first goal in their last-32 win over Ivory Coast.

He was also a second half substitute in his side’s 2-1 extra-time loss to England in the quarter-finals.



SunSport understands that Leipzig are holding firm on a £51million valuation for Nusa, who notched four goals and three assists in 31 Bundesliga appearances last season.

Arsenal are approaching the situation strategically and waiting to assess incoming offers for Gabriel Martinelli before making a formal move.

While the Gunners are not actively pushing to sell Martinelli, a bid exceeding £51m from Europe or Asia could be enough to let the 25-year-old Brazilian go.

Leandro Trossard has already been sold to Besiktas this summer, while Christos Tzolis arrived for £34m from Club Brugge.

Arsenal chief Mikel Arteta missed out on top target Morgan Rogers, with Chelsea sealing a £117m deal.

Neighbours Tottenham are also firmly in the race, but must first clear out their squad before launching an official bid.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Spurs bosses need to resolve the futures of returning loanees Manor Solomon and Mikey Moore, who are both drawing Premier League and Serie A interest.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side have been active in the transfer window already this summer, with Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes signing for £100m and £85m respectively.

Defenders Jan Paul van Hecke – for £52m – and free agents Andy Roberston and Marcos Senesi have also come through the door.

But there is space for a winger, with injured quartet Dejan Kulusevski, Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert missing Spurs’ pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia.

The North London rivals face competition from Serie A giants AC Milan and Roma, who have already opened direct talks with Nusa’s representatives.



Milan have made Nusa a priority target and plan to fund the swoop by selling star man Rafael Leao for around £43m, while Roma are ready to test Leipzig’s resolve with a £38m bid.

Nusa is understood to be open to a fresh challenge after a successful World Cup, which could significantly accelerate discussions in the coming weeks.

But the biggest obstacle for all suitors remains negotiating down Leipzig’s steep price tag during upcoming talks.

Sports.title: From plucky minnows to England heroes, Golden Boot showdown and Viking rows… why the 2026 World Cup was greatest ever
Sports.content:
FIFA’S Team of Tournament features England’s Jude Bellingham, France’s Kylian Mbappe, Argentina’s Lionel Mess . . . and an unlikely hero in Cape Verde’s goalkeeper Vozinha.

The veteran goalie, 40, earned special praise after pulling off a string of eye-catching saves as the minnows suffered a brutal 3-2 defeat to Argentina after extra time.



It was one of the most memorable matches of the tournament, which also featured Viking rows, a barmy Tartan Army and countless Wayne Rooney one-liners.

The memories of this World Cup linger like Donald Trump on the winner’s podium. The doomsters had predicted a dud. Too many teams, too many hydration breaks and way too expensive in a nation likely to shrug its disinterested collective shoulders.



Fifa greed seemed to be throttling the golden goose. Yet, football, as the old school managers liked to say, was the winner.

So how will the 2026 tournament be remembered?

Here, are the best moments. . .

1. Keane’s Shakira nod: It all kicked off with Shakira and Burna Boy belting out the official World Cup song Dai Dai at the opening ceremony in Mexico City.

It wouldn’t be a World Cup without Colombian Shakira gyrating in a grass skirt. This was her fourth.

She also performed at the closing ceremony in New York, with ITV analyst Roy Keane revealing a soft spot for the Hips Don’t Lie singer.



To much sniggering from his fellow pundits, Keane said: “It’s always nice to see Shakira.”

2. A brutal group stage: The group stage was supposed to be a damp squib after Fifa expanded the tournament to 48 teams to allow lower ranked teams to compete. Yet, the minnows defied the odds.

Curacao has a population smaller than Oxford — just 156,000 — and a land mass of just 171 sq miles but secured a point against Ecuador.



The Democratic Republic of Congo — ranked 46th in the world — held Portugal to a draw before giving England a scare in the Round of 32. While Cape Verde — population 525,000 — advanced to the knock-out stage after a 0-0 draw against Champions-to-be Spain.

Its goalie Vozinha, who wasn’t even contracted to a club, became a hero for his string of saves.

In the last 32, he faced off against Lionel Messi and gave Argentina a real scare.

3. Beckham’s fishbowl of wine: In the stands to watch Scotland’s trouncing by Brazil in the group stage was David Beckham, who was caught swigging from what one BBC viewer described as a “fishbowl” of red wine.

Another fan said: “Did everyone see Beckham take the biggest swig of red wine from the biggest glass ever?”



4. Victoria’s sour face: Later in the tournament, Becks defended wife Victoria as she failed to celebrate Jude Bellingham’s crucial equaliser in the Quarter Final 2-1 win against Norway.

Posh Spice, who was sitting next to her more animated hairdresser Ken Paves, seemed to be staring distractedly into the mid-distance and not even looking at the pitch.

Former Three Lions skipper David later said: “She was celebrating inside I promise, her reactions were slightly slower than mine.”

5. Wonderwall: Meanwhile, Oasis’s 1995 hit anthem has become a thing. When Wonderwall was first played after England beat Croatia 4-2, the players looked genuinely moved by England fans’ raucous sing-along.



5 WINNERS Oasis: Their 1995 hit Wonderwall has re-entered the charts across the globe after being adopted by the England team and fans. Djed Spence: No one had England ace Spence becoming a breakout World Cup star. Cape Verde: A minnow that drew with big fish Spain and also ran Argentina close. Boston Landlords: Thirsty Scotland fans swamped the city for pre-match refreshment, and England fans were also in town. Rodri: Spain star won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player. No commentary is complete without a pundit now musing: “Why can’t England produce a midfielder like Rodri?”

6. Barmy Tartan Army: Scotland fans will never be forgotten in Boston after drinking the city dry, while the Netherlands’ Oranje Army swamped Kansas City in memorable scenes.

7. Tuchel the ‘sex symbol’: If England Manager Thomas Tuchel didn’t realise what a white-knuckle ride his job is before the tournament, he does now.

Hailed as a genius for beating Croatia — he told his players at half-time, “If we lose, we lose in our way” — he even became a Mumsnet sex symbol.

A poster asked whether users of the website found him “strangely attractive,” saying he had a “lovely smile when being interviewed after today’s match”.

One user replied: “He has a certain wiry, athletic, long-limbed vibe to him.”



8. Mexican madness: Then there was the Azteca Stadium in Mexico City.

England secured a dramatic victory after facing the altitude, thunder storms and a player sent off.

Defender ‘Big’ Dan Burn came and headed a ball from his own box to well beyond the halfway line. Again, Tuchel lapped up the plaudits.

Then came the downfall as Tuchel’s game management against Argentina in the Semi Final went to pot. But he’ll always have Mumsnet.

9. Anthony Barry: His assistant manager Anthony Barry burst into the national consciousness for his heart-on-the-sleeve half-time interviews. Against Croatia he told viewers that England were “playing with fear”.



5 LOSERS Germany: Penalty kings Germany crashed out to Paraguay in the last 32 – on penalties. VAR: The ref-aiding technology became known as VARgentina after it give Lionel Messi’s men a stream of seemingly favourable decisions. Argentina: Standing with their backs to Spain as they collected the World Cup ­trophy was shameful and pathetic. Panama: It was the highest-scoring World Cup tournament ever played, with 308 goals over a record 104 matches. None of them were scored by Panama, the only team that didn’t find the net. Match-Going Fans: Hotels, transport and match tickets were hiked wildly.

As England led France 4-0 in the third place play-off, he said: “I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words about how proud I am of those players.”

10. Wayne Rooney: In the TV studios, Wayne burst on to the scene like he had as a player at Euro 2004.

His summation of the closing ceremony as “crap” had heads nodding across the land. Over on ITV, Emma Hayes was the stand out, introducing the word “diagonality” into many people’s footballing lexicon.

11. Gianni’s grin: Fifa chief Gianni Infantino’s grinning mug seemed to stare out from the stands at most games. In fact, he travelled for nearly 60,000 miles to take in 44 matches. On 13 occasions he went to two matches on the same day.



12. Playing cards: Fifa was accused of “crossing a line” and putting the sport’s integrity into question, after it overturned a ban on the US’s star player Folarin Balogun for a red card.

It emerged that American President Donald Trump had called Infantino and told him the card was “horrible” and that it was “not a foul”.

The US were duly trounced 4-1 by Belgium in the Quarter Final to provide some sporting justice.

The Belgians celebrated by trolling Trump by mimicking his up-pumping trademark jig.

One social media user said: “Fantastic s***housery.”



13. Legends assemble: Apart from Ronaldo, who looked ready to join a pensioners’ walking football team, all the other big dogs turned up.

10 CELEBS Brad Pitt took in several games wearing a USA shirt. Tom Cruise joined the Beckhams for the USA’s match against Paraguay. Jessica Alba took selfies with her daughters at USA v Turkey, which was also watched by Paris Hilton and her kids. Matt Damon was pictured with wife Luciana at the Final as were superstars Jay-Z and Beyonce. The rapper was also at Ivory Coast v Ecuador. Ryan Reynolds cheered on his home country Canada as they played Bosnia & Herzegovina. Sabrina Carpenter watched Ecuador v Germany through opera glasses. Javier Bardem and Penelope Cruz celebrated Spain’s match winner against Belgium. Timothee Chalamet was pictured kissing Kylie Jenner at the Final.

Messi, Mbappe, Bellingham, Haaland, France’s Ousmane Dembele and Harry Kane scrambled to claim the Golden Boot. Kylian triumphed.

14. Haaland the Viking: Erling won over America with his goofy Viking routine as he did Dallas in a stetson and cowboys boots.

Then he took a stuffed raccoon home on the plane with him.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

15. Aggy Argentina: And then there was the Final. If your child’s under-six team behaved like Argentina’s whingeing brats, you’d take the ball off them and send them home.

Sports.title: Conference League clash SUSPENDED for extreme weather with players forced off pitch
Sports.content:
A EUROPA Conference League qualifier between Aluminij and Dinamo City was suspended after lightning and torrential rain forced players off the pitch in Slovenia.

Reports in Slovenia confirmed the second qualifying round clash at Ljudski Vrt was halted in the 55th minute after dangerous weather swept across the stadium.



Both teams, coaching staff and the match officials immediately retreated to the dressing rooms and tunnel as lightning strikes were detected in the area.

The visitors held a narrow 1-0 lead when play was stopped, with the weather making it unsafe for the match to continue.



Updates posted on X confirmed the suspension was caused by “adverse weather”, with heavy rain and lightning striking close to the ground.

Supporters inside the stadium were left waiting as officials monitored conditions before deciding whether it was safe for the game to resume.

Fortunately, the delay lasted only around 20 minutes.

A further update confirmed the match had resumed once the storm had passed over the stadium.

Dinamo City returned to the pitch still protecting their slender advantage over the Slovenian hosts.

The Albanian side had taken the lead after just 15 minutes when Hekuran Berisha capitalised on a huge defensive mistake.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Aluminij defender Dino Šimunić under-hit a back pass towards goalkeeper Florijan Radu, allowing Berisha to intercept before rounding the keeper and calmly slotting into an empty net.

It proved to be the only shot on target of the opening half as Aluminij struggled to create chances.

Reports in Slovenia also noted the hosts had failed to score in an official match for more than 500 minutes heading into the contest.

The dramatic weather delay came on a busy night of UEFA Conference League qualifying, with three Slovenian clubs all in European action.



But while Bravo battled Škendija and Koper took on Runavik, it was the clash between Aluminij and Dinamo City that was brought to a standstill by Mother Nature before eventually getting back underway.

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe has contract terminated just four months after England icon landed first managerial job
Sports.content:
JERMAIN DEFOE says he is “really disappointed” after his first job in management ended after only SIX competitive matches.

The Premier League legend, 43, has left Woking by mutual consent just four months on from his appointment.



Defoe guided the non-league minnows to a tenth place finish in the National League after taking charge.

But the former Tottenham and West Ham striker has quit the Cards despite overseeing the early stages of pre-season.



In a statement released on social media, Defoe said: “Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking.

“Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.



“I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

“I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club.

“I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for.

“The group is a fantastic one and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

“My time at Woking has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.”

Defoe’s reign got underway with an entertaining 3-3 draw with Eastleigh before winning two of the next five showdowns.

A club statement read: “Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and first team manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.



“We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future.

“The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support.”

Defoe, who bagged a brace in England’s Soccer Aid win last month, had been preparing Woking for their season opener against Sutton United.



But his shock exit means the Cards are now searching for the England icon’s successor ahead of the National League campaign getting underway on August 8.

Sports.title: ‘Exhausted’ Erling Haaland and Wag don pyjama-style outfits as they party in millionaire’s playground Saint-Tropez
Sports.content:
ERLING Haaland and his Wag looked like good bedfellows in pyjama and nightie-style outfits as they partied in millionaire’s playground Saint-Tropez.

The Norwegian scoring sensation has been winding down on the French Riviera with fiancee Isabel Haugseng Johansen after he bagged seven goals at the World Cup.



And the Man City star has enjoyed a fun-filled holiday, during which he has celebrated his 26th birthday.

He spent an hour on a jet ski while Isabel soaked up the sun on the beach.



And he partied at club &ME with his former City teammate Riyad Mahrez, to the delight of revellers.

Fun-loving Haaland went behind the DJ decks and even donned a Viking horns helmet as he lapped up the attention from the crowd.



An onlooker said: “Erling must be exhausted from his World Cup heroics but he’s shown no signs of it.

“He’s been having a great time with Isabel and their friends.



“He loves to have fun and experience life to the fullest.”

The pair, who have a one-year-old son, enjoyed a break in Sicily before visiting Saint-Tropez.

Haaland’s goal-scoring exploits took Norway to their best ever World Cup finish — reaching the quarter-finals, where England knocked them out.



His clinical finishing, including two against Brazil, earned him a place in Fifa’s 2026 World Cup Dream XI.

Sports.title: Why Arsenal splashed £34m on former Norwich flop Christos Tzolis who models his game on World Cup winner
Sports.content:
ARSENAL new boy Christos Tzolis models his game on legendary Spain forward David Villa.

And the Gunners will hope the Greek winger can add goals to their attack after splashing out £34million to sign him on a five-year deal from Club Brugge.



Tzolis, 24, flopped during a spell at Norwich from 2021 to 2024 – but rebuilt his career having moved to Belgium.

He boasted 43 goals and 45 assists in 108 games over his two seasons with Brugge.



But, after winning Belgium’s player of the season last term, Tzolis revealed his inspiration is former Barcelona and Valencia attacker Villa.

Arsenal have signed Tzolis to primarily play off the left and as a replacement for Leandro Trossard, who joined Besiktas this month for £17m.

But – like Trossard – he can also operate as a No 10 and a big part of his game is cutting inside to cause chaos.

Tzolis was ranked first for dribbles completed in the Belgian top flight last season, while setting up more chances than any other player.

And 52 of the 135 chances he created in the league last term were from dead-ball situations – music to the ears of Gunners set-piece coach Nicolas Jover.

He has taken the No 17 shirt at Arsenal – famously worn by Alexis Sanchez – and his stocky frame and eye for goal are reminiscent of the Chilean.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Tzolis has already featured in pre-season friendlies with Club Brugge. It means he can hit the ground running ahead of their first friendly a week on Saturday in Girona.

WHAT THE PLAYER HAS SAID



Tzolis declared: “It’s absolutely amazing to sign for such a big club – the champions of England. I’m very proud to be part of this team.

“When my agent was saying maybe it was a possibility, I was already excited.

“Afterwards it was getting more serious and now I’m here. I had a nice conversation [with Mikel Arteta]. It was around an hour.



“We talked about everything – about the club, about myself, his plans, about the team. It was only positive things.”

On legend Villa – Spain’s all-time top scorer – Tzolis added: “He was a bit more of a striker but I am in this kind of position to play close to the striker and have the opportunity to score.

“I’m a direct player and go for goals or assists. That’s my point of view as an attacker.

“I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my team-mates. And I can say I work hard for the team in the defensive part, too.”



WHAT SPORTING DIRECTOR ANDREA BERTA SAID

The Italian declared: “We are delighted to have completed the signing of Christos.

“Christos is an extremely versatile attacking player who naturally operates on the left but is also comfortable across the front line.

“He’s an excellent finisher with both feet, thrives in tight spaces and possesses incredible technical ability.

“Christos produced outstanding numbers in terms of goals and assists in the last three seasons.

“He’ll raise the technical level of our squad, while bringing positive energy, enthusiasm and a strong mentality to our team.

Sports.title: Man Utd add Nottingham Forest flop and World Cup star to transfer shortlist – but may NOT buy another midfielder
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are considering a shock move for Danilo after also being given fresh hope of landing Aurelien Tchouameni.

The Red Devils bolstered their midfield options by sealing a bargain deal for Youri Tielemans earlier this month.



United chief Michael Carrick has also splashed £50million on Andrey Santos and brought in goalkeeper Karl Darlow ahead of the new season.

Old Trafford chiefs are prepared to bring in more reinforcements – leading to Danilo, 25, being added to their transfer shortlist.



The Botafogo man flopped during his previous spell in the Premier League, only making 62 appearances for Nottingham Forest.

But, having been handed four World Cup outings before Brazil were knocked out by Norway, Danilo has been pinpointed as a possible recruit.



United, who pulled out of a move for international team-mate Ederson, face competition for an agreement.

Newcastle hold an interest in luring Danilo back to England, while Palmeiras and Zenit St Petersburg have tabled bids worth in the region of £25m.

Sports.title: Arsenal preparing £70MILLION transfer bid for Bruno Guimaraes after star, 28, told Newcastle he wants to join Gunners

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog for Thursday, July 23.

Liverpool are facing a crucial summer under new head coach Andoni Iraola and amid the backdrop of takeover talks, the former Cherries boss wants transfers.

The Reds made an approach for PSG target Maghnes Akliouche with the Parisiens unable to meet the demands of Ligue 1 rivals AS Monaco. Meanwhile, Liverpool are said to be leading the race to sign Bradley Barcola, a move which would be another blow for Arsenal, who are also rumoured to hold an interest.

There's a month to go until the Premier League returns, and with pre-season getting underway across the division, the transfer action is picking up. Chelsea completed a deal to sign England star Morgan Rogers after footing up a £117million fee to set the pace for the summer while Alejandro Garnacho has joined Aston Villa on loan.

Arsenal have welcomed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, but their bid to sign Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes is stealing the headlines. The Magpies remain adamant that their captain is not for sale but could they see an Alexander Isak repeat?

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer

Manchester United want to sign a third midfielder before the summer transfer window closes but they've been priced out of a move for Bournemouth star Alex Scott

View 2 Images Danilo played for Brazil at the World Cup (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a move for ex-Nottingham Forest star Danilo. The news comes after United decided not to pursue a deal for Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

‌



Bournemouth will demand at least £70million for Scott, who was the subject of a £64m bid from Chelsea which was rejected earlier this week. United value the England international at around £40m and will now look at alternative options in their search for a third new central midfielder.

‌



BBC Sport report that the Red Devils have registered their interest in Danilo, who plays for Brazilian side Botafogo. It's added that Newcastle were interested in the 25-year-old earlier this summer.

‌



Danilo made four appearances at the World Cup - all from the bench - as part of Carlo Ancelotti's squad. Botafogo have already received two offers in the region of £25m from Brazilian rivals Palmeiras and Russian heavyweights Zenit St Petersburg.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges READ MORE :

Palmeiras, where Danilo made his name over three seasons, are currently pushing hardest to complete a deal. Botafogo would prefer sell him abroad, having paid £21.7m to sign him from Forest a year ago.

‌



Danilo is one of several options for United, who've also enquired about Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni. The Red Devils have already recruited two midfielders this summer; Andrey Santos for £50m and Youri Tielemans for £35m.

In two-and-a-half years with Forest, Danilo made 62 appearances across all competitions. His third season at the City Ground was blighted by a serious ankle injury which took a toll on him.

Which midfielder should Manchester United sign? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Danilo spent two years at Nottingham Forest before joining Botafogo (Image: Cameron Smith - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"It was really tough at first, but with time it got easier," Danilo told FIFA's website before the World Cup. "I started to understand things differently. I matured a lot.

"I became stronger and learned to think more positively every day. After that injury, I developed this mindset."

Article continues below

Botafogo are having a middling season, sitting 10th in the Brazilian top flight with seven wins, four draws and seven defeats after 18 games. Danilo has been prolific in front of goal, though, scoring seven league goals as well as three in cup competitions.

Sports.title: Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges

Manchester United are interested in signing Aurelien Tchouameni from Real Madrid, lodging an enquiry as they bid to revamp their midfield in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Real Madrid are open to selling Aurelien Tchouameni in a major boost to Manchester United's chances of signing him. Tchouameni, 26, has just got back from helping France reach the semi-finals of the World Cup, playing an integral role in Didier Deschamps' side.

‌



But throughout the tournament, his future at club level was a hot topic. United have a long-standing interest in Tchouameni, who Real boss Jose Mourinho initially planned to keep after returning to the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



However, the Sun report that Real are now prepared to let the midfielder go at the right price. The La Liga giants have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and might need to drum up funds.

‌



United's interest is said to have ramped up since the World Cup ended, with Tchouameni out of contract in 2028. It was reported in Spain earlier this month that Real and the Frenchman had agreed a new five-year deal, although there's been no confirmation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

United have already signed two midfielders this summer, paying a combined £85m for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. But with Manuel Ugarte expected to miss most of the season because of a serious knee injury, the Red Devils want to add a third.

‌



Their search for a specialist defensive midfielder has led them to Tchouameni, whose experience of starting the 2022 World Cup final and winning the Champions League in 2024 appeals to United. The former Monaco star also suits United's preferred age range for signings - between 22 and 26.

How much should Manchester United pay for Aurelien Tchouameni? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni's contract with Real Madrid expires in 2028 (Image: Marcel Bonte/Soccrates/Getty Images)

‌



Real's pursuit of Rodri could therefore prove to be a double boost for United, as local rivals City would be losing one of their best players. However, Los Blancos could wait until Rodri's contract expires next summer and sign him on a free.

As for Tchouameni, ex-Real midfielder and French compatriot Claude Makelele has warned Bernabeu chiefs not to sell him. Makelele told DAZN: "He was the only player who performed consistently from start to finish.

"Mourinho isn't a fool; he's a good manager, one of the best managers. He knows he's going to need a strong squad to be able to win La Liga."

Sports.title: Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance
Sports.content:
Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance

Bruno Guimaraes has emerged as a top target for Arsenal this summer in their search for quality reinforcements and they are ready to pay out £70million to sign him

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are poised to table a £70million bid for Bruno Guimaraes - but will not overpay for the midfielder if Newcastle try to resist a sale.

‌



The Gunners are in the market for quality additions to bolster the squad that won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final last season. And a move for Guimaraes, who boasts extensive top-flight pedigree, appeals in their search for an elite midfielder.

‌



Guimaraes, 28, is known to be keen on the move, which would give him a realistic opportunity to win major trophies.

‌



Newcastle, though, have no appetite to cash in on their talismanic captain — and it remains to be seen if a financial package in the region of £70m would realistically be enough for them to soften that stance.

BBC Sport report that Arsenal are ready to launch an official bid of that amount after stepping up their interest in Guimaraes. However, it's noted that they will not stray from their valuation of the Brazilian.

Whether or not they would consider bidding higher for a player who turns 29 later this year remains to be seen. And if that is the case, then they could opt to move on to other targets.

‌



That stance saw them miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers, a long-term target who was viewed as the ceiling-raiser signing Arsenal were looking for in their search for a new left-sided attacker.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes wants to join Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

The Gunners valued Rogers at £80m; a figure far lower than Aston Villa's valuation of the England star. That gulf in valuations opened the door for Chelsea to swoop in with a £117m offer. Arsenal declined to match it, with Rogers going on to join one of their big domestic rivals.

Article continues below

Rogers' former Aston Villa team-mate, Ezri Konsa, is another player Arsenal are courting with the new Premier League season now just weeks away.

Sports.title: Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook
Sports.content:
Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook

Lionel Messi and his beaten Argentina team-mates deserved all the flak that came their way following the World Cup final but that should not give Gianni Infantino and FIFA a reprieve

View 3 Images Lionel Messi has come under fire for his behaviour in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

According to a polling company that might have better things to do, Lionel Messi’s popularity amongst British people has gone down since he tried to get the saintly Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final. It is unclear whether this news is keeping Messi awake at night but you suspect not.

‌



Messi’s lamentable attempt to land Cucurella in trouble was part of a tapestry of unedifying Argentinian antics and was unbecoming of a great player. But it was hardly the crime of the century.

‌



Since when did we become so puritanical? Would Cucurella have done it if the situation of the game had been reversed? Of course he would.

‌



You might hold Messi to a higher moral standard but players trying to get opponents into bother is a staple of the modern game. It did not help Messi’s cause that he was the captain of a squad that turned its back on Spain’s coronation after it had also descended into violent disarray at the final whistle.

Argentina flop's sister makes Falklands Islands claim after World Cup shame READ MORE :

The offending individuals will deserve whatever punishment comes their way and deserved all the criticism that has already come their way. But let’s not pretend we were shocked by the Argentinian reaction to the loss to Spain.

And let’s not allow their behaviour to deflect criticism and scrutiny from where it most needs to be directed most. It needs to be directed most at Gianni Infantino and FIFA.

‌



View 3 Images Bryson DeChambeau threatened to get Donald Trump involved in his rules row at The Open (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

When it comes to petulant reactions, there was a belter at Royal Birkdale last Friday after Bryson DeChambeau received a two-shot penalty for what was a debatable rules infringement. It was a slightly controversial decision but one DeChambeau should have taken on the chin.

Instead, he ranted and raved at officials … and, apparently, threatened to call Donald Trump and get him involved. As it happened, the President of the United States never stepped in but you know where the idea came from.

‌



Thankfully, at least one football association is taking a stance. The Norwegians, headed by its federation president Lise Klaveness, are set to make an official complaint to FIFA’s ethics committee over Trump’s involvement in the Folarin Balogun case, which saw the American striker have his red card ban suspended.

View 3 Images Messi has been accused of trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off (Image: AFP or licensors)

Hopefully, more will follow suit. And hopefully, more will tell the relevant committee that the hydration breaks were aberrations that cannot be repeated. Hopefully, more will kick up a serious fuss over ticket prices and already demand changes for the 2030 World Cup.

‌



Never mind the tantrums shown by several Argentinians after the last whistle - and it has to be said that we seem to be more upset by them than the Spanish are - the final itself was a grotesquely gaudy and elongated occasion. Wayne Rooney had it spot on when he said the best thing about the half-time show was when it finished.

Sure, Argentina’s behaviour needs to be punished. And sure, Messi did not cover himself in glory. But the people who really need to be looked at now the World Cup is over are Infantino and FIFA.

Sports.title: Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers

A lot has changed since Manchester United last met Rosenborg

View 2 Images Less than half of the starters from Manchester United's previous trip to Rosenborg still play for the club (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are due to take on Rosenborg this week, some two years on from their last meeting. Those two years have been incredibly eventful, though, with the Premier League club undergoing a huge upheaval - and not just with the playing staff.

‌



Erik ten Hag was still United's manager when that match in Trondheim took place. He had just led the Red Devils to FA Cup glory but pre-season got off to a tough start when Noah Holm scored the winner in Trondheim.

‌



Ten Hag was gone just months later with Ruben Amorim taking his place. However, the Portuguese coach only lasted 14 months in the hotseat before his January 2026 exit, meaning Michael Carrick is in charge for the latest trip to Norway.

‌



Changes in the dugout have also been accompanied by an overhaul of the playing staff. Six of the 11 players who started the last Rosenborg game have since left or retired, while two more could yet leave Old Trafford before the current window is up.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design READ MORE :

Radek Vitek started in goal that day and is the sole survivor of the back five still on the books at Old Trafford. The Czech started behind centre-back Jonny Evans - now retired and part of Carrick's coaching staff - and three other defenders now playing elsewhere.

‌



Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Will Fish both left the following month and could end up facing one another in the Championship before too long. Wan-Bissaka's West Ham are newly relegated to the second tier while Fish's Cardiff won promotion last season.

The defence was rounded out by academy graduate Sam Murray, who left for Carlisle in 2025 and is now looking for a new club again. As for Vitek, a promise of first team football could tempt him away.

View 2 Images Aaron Wan-Bissaka left United just a month after the friendly in Norway (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so," he said after featuring against Wrexham in United's first friendly of the summer. "I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Further forward, Casemiro gave United two more years but left in the summer of 2026. The Brazilian is now at Inter Miami, with a strong end to last season not enough to keep him around.

He played in midfield with Mason Mount and Hannibal Mejbri that day. While Mount is still a United player, impressing against Wrexham, Hannibal is long gone.

‌



The Tunisian international sealed a permanent move to Burnley in August 2024 and remains at Turf Moor to this day. He helped the Clarets win promotion to the Premier League but they dropped straight back down last term.

Pre-season regularly gives clubs the opportunity to blood younger talent, particularly while waiting for international players to return from major tournaments. Ethan Williams and Ethan Wheatley are both still at United, having started that Rosenborg game, as are some of the youngsters who came off the bench in Trondheim.

Completing the front three was Marcus Rashford, who had surprisingly been overlooked by Gareth Southgate for England's Euro 2024 squad. The forward spent the 2025/26 season on loan at Barcelona but his future is up in the air again after the Catalan club opted against triggering a buy option, and manager Carrick will have a decision to make on the academy graduate.

Sports.title: Christos Tzolis: How Arsenal's new £34m signing went from Norwich flop to Champions League star
Sports.content:
It says everything about the evolution of Christos Tzolis that Arsenal's newest signing accrued more goal contributions last year than he made league appearances across an ill-fated spell at Norwich City.

The reason Tzolis will play for the newly minted Premier League champions is because, at 24, he is now every inch the clinical, cold-blooded attacker that Europe's elite believed he would become back when he was a teenager. Barcelona were among his illustrious courters back then as heavyweights flocked to observe a prodigious talent. But it was Norwich, rather than Barcelona, who clinched the youngster's sought-after signature.

The Tzolis hype train was already in full flow when the formalities of his £8.8million transfer from PAOK was confirmed back in the summer of 2021. At 21, Tzolis was already a full Greece international; for a Norwich side who were back in the big-time after romping to the Championship title under Daniel Farke, the winger's capture had all the hallmarks of a transfer coup.

And yet, things deteriorated rapidly. After scoring twice in a 6-0 win over Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup on his debut, Tzolis soon fell out of favour. By early November, Tzolis had seen the manager who signed him sacked by the club, just hours after recording Norwich's first league win of the season.

‌



Dean Smith's appointment as Farke's successor proved to be the catalyst for the change of shape which effectively killed Tzolis' Norwich career.

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

“It was the hardest year of my career,” Arsenal's newest attacker conceded to Het Nieuwsblad back in 2024. “The first time I didn’t play with the first team, but with the second [reserves], I was very disappointed. That was the lowest point of my career.

“My agent and my family had to convince me not to give up. And life off the pitch wasn’t easy back then.”

In total, Tzolis made just 27 appearances for Norwich before leaving the club permanently in the summer of 2024. The first of two loan spells designed to resurrect his career, with FC Twente, fell flat due to a knee injury. It was in the second tier of German football with Fortuna Dusseldorf that the youngster finally rediscovered his killer instinct, plundering more than 20 goals.

‌



From there, he never looked back. Unsurprisingly, Dusseldorf triggered their option to sign him permanently for just £3m. But it was Tzolis' next move which put the teen prodigy back on the path to superstardom.

Club Brugge swooped in to offer Dusseldorf the chance to effectively double their money instantly. They accepted and, in Belgium, Tzolis has flourished, accumulating more than 20 goals in successive seasons. Not only did he score 22 times last term, he registered a staggering 29 assists to break out as one of the biggest stars in the Belgian Pro League.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has transformed into a different player with Club Brugge (Image: JASPER JACOBS, BELGA MAG/AFP via Getty Images)

Tzolis returns to these shores not only hardened by the challenges of his stint in Norfolk, but brimming with confidence. Deadly with his right-foot, he has thrived in a left-sided attacking role and is viewed as the successor to the revered Leandro Trossard, who completed a move to Besiktas last week.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Norwich's sporting director at the time Tzolis was signed, Stuart Webber, cites the physicality of the Premier League as one of the reasons behind the young attacker's failure to live up to expectations. “He was very young, coming into the hardest league in the world where the physicality is off the charts,” said Webber.

“It didn’t work out because we [Norwich] were a struggling team in an unforgiving division. Attacking players don’t get 100 touches of the ball when they are playing for Norwich. If he’d been at an Arsenal he would have probably been successful straight away.”

Tzolis returns to the Premier League a different beast. Naturally, he has grown physically and looks more robust than the twinkle-eyed teenager who was swatted aside both figuratively and literally at Norwich. The numbers he has put up consistently elsewhere in Europe, albeit at a level which is not elite, are eye-catching. His previous experience, although chastening, should give him some form of advantage when it comes to adapting to the rigours of Premier League life this time around.

“I’m a direct player, I go for goals or assists,” Tzolis told Arsenal’s website. “That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.”

‌



View 3 Images Christos Tzolis struggled previously in the Premier League for Norwich City (Image: Ryan Pierse)

Arsenal went into the summer with designs on levelling up their attack, particularly on the left side. A deal for Morgan Rogers is now off the table, and Tzolis will not be the only acquisition in that area. Whereas at Tzolis organically became the main man at Brugge, his role at Arsenal will be significantly different.

There is, of course, the risk that Tzolis' exceptional record in Belgium does not translate to the Premier League. Even with the additional experience and nous under his belt.

In a transfer market where the Premier League's heavyweights have focused on domestic signings for inflated transfer fees this summer, the signing of Tzolis is somewhat of an outlier.

‌



But considering the transfer fee, the prospective upsides to the deal and the fact Arsenal are still after a ceiling-raiser signing for the left wing berth, you can see why signing Tzolis is a risk they feel is worth taking.

Sports.title: 'Kings of Manchester' - Elliot Anderson taunts Man Utd as City unveil £116m signing
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson hasn't even kicked a ball in anger on behalf of the blue side of Manchester.

But the England superstar has guaranteed that most of the fury will belong to those on the red half, having pinned his colours well and truly to the Manchester City mast. Anderson snubbed Manchester United in favour of becoming City's most expensive signing in a £116m deal. And he's wasted no time in making it clear why he chose one neighbour over the other.

“I think they're winners. They're relentless - and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of," said Anderson. "Champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join.

"For as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

Anderson’s comments will rile his new neighbours and echo the time when City taunted United with a giant ‘Welcome To Manchester’ poster depicting the face of Carlos Tevez, having lured the Argentine from Old Trafford in 2009.

United might have spent months attempting to land Anderson themselves, but the player insists Sir Jim Ratcliffe & Co were wasting their time.

Former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson once labelled City the ‘noisy neighbours’. But City have gone on to dominate the landscape of English football in the last decade.

‌



View 2 Images Carlos Tevez was welcomed to Man City in quite the fashion (Image: PA Archive/Press Association Images)

Anderson said: "Manchester City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen. As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity.

"From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. The success they have had, and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It’s a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that."

Anderson's rise to the top has been rapid and phenomenal. In the space of four seasons he has gone from being on-loan with Bristol Rovers to helping England reach a World Cup semi final, via becoming the most expensive footballer in Britain.

‌



But taking the next step at club level is something Anderson is relishing, because he knows he has joined a machine made to be successful.

He said: "It's happened quite quick, but I think I always believed that I could get to this point - and this is where I want to be. Now that I'm here, I'll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.

"It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer. I'm so happy to have been given this opportunity, and I am determined to repay the faith City have shown in me."

‌



Anderson, 23, grew up marvelling at the influence Kevin De Bruyne once had on City and English football. And he admits now finding himself on the same team De Bruyne used to grace with such distinction, feels like a dream come true.

He said: "I think Kevin De Bruyne is someone who I've hugely looked up to over the past seven or eight years.

"I've always grown up through the academy at Newcastle. I've always wanted to play like him. I've watched him all the time, and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special."

Pep Guardiola might now be gone, but Anderson is relishing working under Enzo Maresca. Not to mention the chance to prove he is worth the nickname the 'Geordie Maradona', given to him by Rovers fans during his time in Bristol.

‌



He added: "They started that and it sort of stuck everywhere I've been. It's a really good one.

"It makes me happy when I hear it on the pitch and yeah, it gives me real confidence.

"I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, I bring physicality, energy. I'd like to think I'd get them (City fans) excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team."

Sports.title: Rovers fight from 12 points behind to claim derby win at Hull FC
Sports.content:
Hull FC 20-34 Hull KR: Rovers fight from 12 points behind to claim Super League derby victory and move back into playoff spots

Hull KR picked up a ninth derby victory over Hull FC in a row, battling from 12-0 behind to win on Thursday

Defending Super League champions Hull KR moved back into the playoff positions following a 34-20 comeback derby victory at Hull FC from 12 points behind.

Hull FC, who had lost eight derbies in a row heading into this one, started superbly to score twice within the opening eight minutes through Joe Batchelor and Davy Litten for a 12-0 lead.

Yet, Rovers battled back to level by half-time following tries from Tom Amone and Arthur Mourgue.

The Black and Whites briefly led again at 14-12 in the second half via the boot of Zak Hardaker, but a try from Jack Broadbent and penalty from Mourgue soon put the Robins six points ahead.

The match then swung on the next try with 12 minutes to play; Hull FC seemingly ready to score down the right, but Joe Burgess pinching an intercept to race nearly 80 metres down the field for Hull KR's fourth.

Mourgue added another penalty to stretch the lead further, with Jake Arthur's late try for Hull FC academic in the end as Jordan Dezaria forced his way over for another Hull KR effort late in the game.
