(Photo source: ROMATSA on Facebook)

World.title: Bucharest exhibitions: Pop art, photos by Cristian Mungiu at upcoming season of Art Safari
World.content:
The upcoming season of Art Safari will host exhibitions dedicated to pop art, the reality of climate change, and photography by filmmaker Cristian Mungiu, in addition to a show focused on Brâncuși, the organizers announced.

The exhibition Brâncuși and His Muses, curated by Doina Lemny, looks at the artist’s relationships with the women in his life: artists, writers, dancers and gallery owners who frequented his Paris studio. Among them are Baroness Renée Irana Frachon (the model for Sleeping Muse), Margit Pogány (the model for Mademoiselle Pogany), Lizica and Irina Codreanu, artist and writer Nancy Cunard, poet Mina Loy, dancers Marthe Lebherz, Florence Meyer and Marina Saliapin, as well as the sculptor's partner, British-born pianist Vera Moore.

The exhibition features a collection of photographs taken by Brâncuși, films, correspondence, posters, personal documents, and items that belonged to his muses, including dresses and jewelry.

The exhibition Pop Art. A World in Color traces the evolution of pop art, from its origins in post-war America to its global influence today.

The exhibition follows the movement through Andy Warhol's Factory, Roy Lichtenstein's comic book-inspired universe, and the visual languages of Keith Haring and Jean-Michel Basquiat. It also explores Nouveau Réalisme, the European response to pop art, and includes works by a new generation of artists who carried Warhol's legacy forward. “Works by internationally acclaimed contemporary artists, such as Takashi Murakami and Damien Hirst, demonstrate how pop art evolved into a global visual language in the 21st century,” a presentation of the show reads.

War and Peace, an exhibition presented in partnership with the National History Museum of Romania, explores “how violence has, for centuries, been invested with meaning, glory and necessity, while peace, though celebrated in ideology, has remained a fleeting and fragile exception in history.”

The New Climate. Are We Ready?, Art Safari’s interactive pavilion, challenges visitors to discover if they are ready to face the challenges brought on by extreme weather events. Once isolated occurrences, these are increasingly becoming part of everyday reality.

The temporary exhibitions pavilion will present Cristian Mungiu. Fjord – Photographs, with photos taken by the Romanian filmmaker during the research phase for the Palme d’Or-winning Fjord.

"Preparing a film is the happiest stage of the entire filmmaking process for me. It's a time when I'm allowed to wander through wonderful places and strike conversations with all kinds of people under the pretext that I'm working. During those periods I take many photographs, not only for the film that will eventually reach the screen, but also for the most wonderful film of all: of my life making films. I haven’t managed yet to tell that story properly, but I begin for now with these photographs taken while researching for Fjord,” the director explains.

The next season of Art Safari takes place from September 18 to December 20. The exhibition of photos by Mungiu is open from September 18 to November 2.

(All images: Art Safari)

World.title: Romanian Irina Stoian appointed chief AI commercial officer at market research firm NielsenIQ
World.content:
Irina Stoian has been appointed chief AI commercial officer at NielsenIQ, one of the world's largest market research firms and a leader in the consumer intelligence segment, with operations in Romania.

The newly-created position is designed to accelerate NIQ’s enterprise AI commercial strategy and help clients turn the company’s AI capabilities into business impact and growth, according to the company press release.

Stoian will help align Product, Technology, Commercial, Partnerships, and Marketing around a unified AI growth strategy. Her remit includes shaping commercial AI offerings, strategic partnerships, pricing and business models, and deeper integration of NIQ capabilities into client workflows.

The appointment builds on NIQ’s broader AI strategy. The company’s AI portfolio includes ConnectAI, NIQ Optiq, and NIQ Cadence.

“AI is not a feature we are adding to NIQ; it is core to our product strategy,” said Jim Peck, Chief Executive Officer of NIQ. “Irina brings exactly the combination of commercial credibility and AI fluency we need to make that strategy land with clients.”

Stoian joins NIQ from Palantir Technologies, where she most recently served as Commercial AI Lead and spent nearly six years helping organizations deploy and scale AI-powered solutions. During her tenure, she held leadership roles spanning AI strategy, commercial operations, go-to-market execution, and enterprise transformation. Before Palantir, she worked at Barclays in analytics and commercialization-focused roles and was recognized by Forbes Romania’s 30 Under 30 program.

“I joined NIQ because it has the rare combination of trusted data, strong products, global scale, exceptional talent, and deep customer relationships needed to be a leader in this next era,” said Irina Stoian.

“As AI continues to evolve rapidly, we created the CAICO role to better connect product strategy, commercialization, and client needs,” said Troy Treangen, Chief AI & Product Officer at NIQ. “Irina will help connect strategy, product, commercial execution, and client needs to translate AI innovation into market impact.”

With operations in more than 90 countries, NIQ covers approximately 82% of the world’s population and more than USD 7.4 trillion in global consumer spend. NIQ has been active in Romania for more than 30 years and currently has more than 300 employees under the NIQ and GfK brands. The two local subsidiaries posted combined revenue of RON 116.7 million last year and a net profit of RON 9.73 million.

World.title: Five feature films, 26 shorts compete at Anonimul Festival in Romania’s Danube Delta
World.content:
A total of 26 short films will compete in the national and international short film competitions, while five feature films will vie for the Anonimul Trophy at the 23rd edition of the Anonimul International Independent Film Festival, set to take place from August 10 to August 16 in Sfântu Gheorghe, in Romania's Danube Delta, the organizers announced.

This year's program includes the feature film competition, national and international short film competitions, special screenings, and Q&A sessions with filmmakers and guests.

"We did not begin the selection process with a predetermined theme. Yet, as the five films came together, one question emerged to connect them: what happens when a person discovers they are living in a world already written for them, by family, authorities, tradition, history, the place where they were born, or even by their own fiction? This year's competition covers five distinct voices that question, challenge and, at times, surprise one another," Ludmila Cvikova, curator of the feature film competition, explained.

All five feature films will be screened in Sfântu Gheorghe after world premieres at major festivals including the one held in Venice, Sundance, Karlovy Vary, Warsaw, Busan, San Francisco and Palm Springs.

The feature film competition includes: Broken Voices, directed by Ondřej Provazník (Czech Republic, Slovakia); Kurak, directed by Emil Atageldiyev and Erke Dzhumakmatova (Kyrgyzstan); If I Go Will They Miss Me, directed by Walter Thompson-Hernandez (United States); The End of the World (Sfârșitul lumii), directed by Sebastian Pereanu (Romania); and Silent Rebellion, directed by Marie-Elsa Sgualdo (Switzerland, Belgium, France)

The winner of the Anonimul Trophy will be chosen by the festival public and will receive a EUR 3,000 prize.

The festival also includes Romanian and international short film competitions. From more than 150 submissions, film critic Ionuț Mareș selected 14 Romanian short films to compete for the EUR 1,000 Audience Award.

The Romanian competition includes: Ajutoare (Benefits), Bunicu doarme (Grandpa Is Sleeping), Cherry Master, Fursecuri și lapte (Cookies and Milk), Go Outside and Hug a Tree, Index, Interferențe (Interference), Lichior de mentă (Mint Liqueur), Mama (Mother), Proprietate privată (Private Property), Rosebuds, Tangent, Viitorul ți-l faci cu mâna ta, dar de ce să nu îl lași pe mâna unor specialiști? (You Shape Your Own Future, but Why Not Leave It to the Experts?), and Vizita (The Visit).

The international competition features 12 films selected from more than 200 entries from around the world. The EUR 1,000 Audience Award for Best International Short Film will be selected from the following entries: Ali (Bangladesh, Philippines); Class Photo (Lithuania); The Cow (Croatia, Montenegro); Dog and Wolf (Czech Republic); Hyena (United States, China); Mal de Madre (Spain); Nest (Switzerland); No Skate! (France); Norheimsund (Cuba, United States); Samba Infinito (Brazil); Someday, a Child (France, Lebanon, Romania); and These Voices Are Real (Iran).

"From troubled relationships to existential and artistic crises, from first sexual discoveries to the death of a family member, from unexpected encounters to life-changing decisions, this year's short film competition explores a wide range of subjects familiar to all of us through bold and engaging filmmaking styles. The international competition is a carousel of emotions and cinematic forms, as well as an audiovisual journey through different societies and cultures full of surprises," Mareș explained.

(Photo: Dragoş Asaftei/ Anonimul)

World.title: Albanian Protesters Clash With Police at Rally Outside Parliament
World.content:
Hundreds of protesters clashed with police in front of parliament on Thursday in the Albanian capital, Tirana, as MPs convened for their last session before the summer holiday.

The clash started when police tried to push a barricade forwards several metres to stop protesters from throwing eggs and tomatoes at MPs’ cars entering the parliaments building. When this attempt to move the protesters away failed, police used pepper spray and water cannon to disperse the rally.

At least one police officer and one protester were injured when stones were thrown. Dozens of protesters were affected by chemicals used in the water cannon; some required medical treatment.

Citizens.al, a local platform promoting civic journalism, said that one of its journalists, Vjolanda Peca, had been arrested while reporting on the protest. “Our editorial office condemns this act and calls on authorities to guarantee that journalists perform their duty freely, safely and without any pressure,” the platform said.

The protest in front of parliament was part of the ongoing rallies nicknamed the “Flamingo Revolution,” which started in opposition to planned tourist developments deemed threatening to bird life and the environment, including a project linked to Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. They have widened to include calls for Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation and an end to the rule of the two political parties that have governed the country for decades.

World.title: Financier-Turned-PM Plans Radical Cure for Moldova’s Ills
World.content:
Moldova’s President, Maia Sandu, rang Vasile Tofan in October last year to try to convince him to leave the private equity company Horizon Capital and become the country’s next prime minister. Tofan declined.

The businessman and economist Alexandru Munteanu took the job instead. When he then resigned on July 3, Sandu offered Tofan the job again. This time, he said yes.

“This time, I gave it a great deal of thought,” Tofan told media outlet Pro TV shortly after parliament approved his government lineup on Tuesday, with backing coming from Sandu’s ruling Action and Solidarity Party, PAS.

“My initial response was immediate: if the governing party believed I could serve my country, I was determined to do so,” he declared.

World.title: Closed Roads Leave Kosovo-Montenegro Mountain Region Cut Off
World.content:
Authorities in Kosovo have blamed the delays to the border demarcation on “technical issues”.

“Once these technical issues are resolved, the Ministry will work to facilitate border traffic,” the government said.

Montenegro’s interior ministry said “there is not a single problem” on its side of the border.

“Over the last decade, several initiatives have been sent to Kosovo authorities through diplomatic channels for the implementation of this Agreement, but there has been no response from their side,” the ministry told BIRN.

“The reasons for the non-implementation of the Agreement lie exclusively on the Kosovo side.”

The consequences, however, are felt on both sides.

Near Velika, a village on the slopes of Cakorr/Cakor mountain near the Lim River, an old military bunker stands as a ruined reminder that this was once a stronghold of the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA.

“The troubled days are behind us, the years lived under the shadow of watchtowers and military outposts are gone, but we need to move freely,” said 56-year-old Vuksan Vuletic, who spends every summer with his family on Cakorr/Cakor mountain. He joined the road protest last month.

“The states must make a decision on this,” Vuletic told BIRN. “It would make a huge difference if this road were reopened for the entire Lim Valley and beyond.”

In Murino, another of the mountain villages, café owner Nedzad Cecunjanin said the city of Peja/Pec in Kosovo was “like a second mother” to people like him.

“We were educated there and relied on it for many of our needs,” he said. “During the war, it was where we found safety. We have many family ties and godparent relationships there. We even have our cemeteries there.”

“But all of that has gradually been disrupted because we have been cut off from Peja/Pec since 1999.”

“We appeal to the governments of Kosovo and Montenegro, as well as the EU and foreign embassies, to help reopen this road as soon as possible,” he said.

Not everyone agrees. Some villagers on the Montenegrin side fear the reopening of the road may lead to Kosovo seeking more land.

Unfinished road

World.title: New Party Brings Fresh Hope – and Risks – for Turkey’s Embattled Opposition
World.content:
“We opened up a new road because they blocked all the others. We are opening up that road now. Are you ready to march to power? We will march to power.”

With these stirring words, Ozgur Ozel told his parliamentary group on July 21 he was leaving the main opposition Republican People’s Party, CHP, to establish a new party.

Its name, logo and other details will be announced at a later date, after which various CHP MPs are expected to join it. An estimated 80 to 90 of the CHP’s 135 MPs are likely to switch sides.

Ozel, who was removed as CHP leader following a controversial court ruling in May, predicted that his new party would immediately become the largest opposition group in parliament.

World.title: Romanian City Holds Out Against Authorising LGBTQ+ Pride March
World.content:
Oradea’s unauthorised Pride March in 2025. Photo: Photo: Ovi D. Pop/Oradea Pride.

Just over 250 kilometres separate Romania’s western city of Oradea from Budapest in Hungary, but until recently the two cities shared another distinction: both had refused to allow Pride marches.

Hungary’s capital hosted a Pride event this year despite government opposition. Oradea is now the only major city in the European Union where local authorities continue to deny permission for a Pride march, after refusing to authorise the 2026 event on Wednesday.

“The City Hall has decided not to approve the event. All 115 possible routes proposed by the organisers are concentrated in the city’s central area … These routes are unavailable because they overlap with other authorised events, or are affected by major public infrastructure works,” municipal spokesperson Octavian Haragoș said, as quoted by the local news outlet ebihoreanul.ro.

The municipality did not explain why alternative routes outside the city centre could not be considered. The decision followed weeks of delays by the city council in ruling on the organisers’ request, where conservative councillors and religious groups dominated the debate.

Human rights groups condemned the decision, arguing that it violates the constitutional right to peaceful assembly.

“We consider this decision completely unacceptable because it effectively blocks people’s constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” Victor Ciobotaru, director of ACCEPT, Romania’s leading LGBTQ+ rights organisation, told BIRN.

“Under Romanian law, local authorities cannot ban a public march. Their role is to identify practical solutions to ensure that such events can take place safely and under appropriate conditions, not to prevent them altogether,” Ciobotaru added.

Citing the same legal argument, ARK Oradea, the organisation behind the city’s Pride Parade, said the march would go ahead on July 25 despite the municipality’s refusal to authorise it.

“Our march will take place … As a sign of solidarity and concern for the situation in Oradea, representatives of nine diplomatic missions accredited to Romania, as well as representatives of the Ombudsman Institution, will be present in Oradea to monitor the unfolding of events,” ARK said, adding that the presence of diplomats reflects growing international concern over restrictions on freedom of assembly and LGBTQ+ rights in Romania.

This marks the fourth consecutive year that Oradea’s authorities have refused to authorise the Pride Parade.

Last year, however, an unauthorised march was still held through the city centre, attended by several hundred mostly young people. There were brief scuffles between some participants and the police but the situation did not escalate.

Authorities later imposed fines totalling 19,800 lei (about 3,900 euros) on organisers and participants in the unauthorised march

Romania has made progress on LGBTQ+ rights since joining the European Union in 2007 but continues to rank among the bloc’s weakest performers in terms of legal protections and social acceptance.

Consensual same-sex relations have been legal since 2001, but same-sex marriage and civil partnerships are not recognised, despite a 2023 ruling by the European Court of Human Rights requiring Romania to provide legal recognition and protection for same-sex couples.

Public attitudes toward LGBTQ+ people remain largely conservative, particularly outside major cities. Pride marches have been held annually in Bucharest for two decades, however, and in several other cities, generally under police protection and without major incidents.

Human rights organisations have urged Romania to strengthen anti-discrimination protections and fully implement European human rights standards, arguing that it is lagging behind in terms of the country’s commitments as an EU member.

World.title: EU, OSCE Missions Criticise Kosovo’s Demolition of Serb-Owned Villas
World.content:
Demolition of villas near Ujman/Gazivoda lake in north Kosovo on July 21, 2026. Photo: BIRN

International missions in Kosovo expressed concern on Wednesday over the police’s demolition of 11 villas belonging to local Serbs near Lake Ujman/Gazivoda in the Serb-majority north of the country.

Kosovo authorities said the houses were built illegally on land owned by the public water management company Iber-Lepenc, near the Ujman/Gazivode Lake. The operation began on June 26.

The European Union Office in Kosovo said that it regretted Tuesday’s demolitions, noting that, “the affected residents had already initiated court proceedings within the 15-day deadline provided in notices issued by the public enterprise Iber-Lepenc to vacate the land”.

The EU called for an “immediate halt to any further demolitions, forced removals or takeovers until concerns relating to due process, proportionality, property rights, human rights and effective remedies are adequately addressed.

“Irreversible enforcement measures in the context of pending proceedings and contested property claims raise serious rule-of-law concerns,” the statement added.

The OSCE Mission in Kosovo said that, “any action affecting property rights, including the demolition of illegally constructed buildings, must be carried out strictly within the applicable legal framework, with full respect for due process”.

The mission said affected individuals should be informed promptly and adequately of the legal basis for actions taken against their property. “The rule of law, transparency, and due process must be applied consistently and without distinction to all illegally constructed buildings across Kosovo,” it said.

It added that enforcement measures against unauthorised construction should follow the same legal standards and procedural safeguards for all communities. “Selective or uneven application of the law, whether real or perceived, risks undermining public confidence and negatively affect inter-community relations and trust,” it said.

Faruk Mujka, chief executive of the state-owned hydro-economic company Iber-Lepenci, wrote on Facebook on Tuesday that “11 illegally constructed villas had been removed during Tuesday’s operation”.

Mujka said the action was carried out by the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure with assistance from the police following a request from Iber-Lepenc to return the property to the company’s management.

Ujman/Gazivoda Lake is considered strategic infrastructure for Kosovo. It supplies drinking water to several cities, supports electricity generation and provides water for irrigation.

Fitore Pacolli, acting minister of the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, noted at the start of demolition work in June that the operation was being conducted to return illegally occupied property in northern Kosovo to the administration of Iber-Lepenc.

“The protection of our water resources remains our highest priority. For this reason, we will continue to protect them, manage them responsibly, and develop them as a vital asset for Kosovo,” Pacolli wrote.

But the Serbian government’s office for Kosovo condemned the operation as a “violent demolition” undertaken “without any court verdict”.

“The owners of the villas found out about the demolition of their property, which they had acquired for years, from the notices that were attached to their buildings, and when they asked for court decisions today, they did not receive them,” it said.

“All this indicates that these demolitions were not carried out with the aim of implementing some kind of law, but for a political reason,” it added.

NOTE: This article was amended on July 22, 2026 to clarify that Faruk Mujka is chief executive of the state-owned hydro-economic company Iber-Lepenci.

World.title: Serbia Indicts Six for Drug Trafficking Linked to North Macedonia
World.content:
Serbia’s Public Prosecutor’s Office for Organised Crime filed an indictment on Tuesday accusing six alleged members of an organised crime group of producing and trafficking drugs within Serbia and North Macedonia during 2025 until January 29, 2026.

The prosecution on Wednesday said the indictment was filed against Aleksandar Mijajlovic as the organiser, Ivan Dragnic as the co-organiser, and Nebojsa Spasojevic, Rade Spasojevic, Uros Mladenovski and Robert Zivkovic as members of the same crime group.

“The evidence collected … indicates that the organisers devised the group’s operational structure, established its hierarchy, assigned roles among its members in advance, and secured the financial resources necessary to carry out the criminal plan,” the prosecution said in a press release.

The group is suspected of transporting nearly five tonnes of marijuana from North Macedonia to Serbia and storing it in residential and commercial premises used by Nebojsa and Rade Spasojevic in the village of Konjuh, near Krusevac, central Serbia, where the drugs were repackaged and prepared for distribution to end-buyers.

Spasojevic was a local official of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, at the time of the bust. Serbian Defence Minister Bratislav Gasic, himself from Krusevac, denied the party was involved and repeated that it was clear that there are “no protected individuals” in Serbia because they had arrested Spasojevic.

The suspects are charged with using the company Alfapharm Group, based in Skopje, as a legitimate business entity to cover the narcotics production.

The company held permits issued by the authorities in North Macedonia to cultivate and produce cannabis extracts for medical purposes.

“The company was misused to conceal the organisation of the procurement, storage, repackaging, and transportation of large quantities of the narcotic drug marijuana,” the press release said.

According to the prosecution, in November 2025, the group organised the procurement of 8,832 kilograms of dried cannabis flower from the supplier CBD Med Plant from Strumica, North Macedonia.

The drugs were stored at the premises of Alfapharm Group, weighed, repackaged and prepared for transportation. The group used documentation relating to the export of textile goods for this during international transport.

The indictment added that Robert Zivkovic is charged with managing storage of the drugs, supervising the packaging process, organising their transportation, and overseeing their unloading and storage in Serbia. Nebojsa and Rade Spasojevic are alleged to have been responsible for receiving, storing, repackaging, and arranging the further transport of the drugs.

Serbian police arrested Uros Mladenovski at the end of January in Belgrade, when he collected around a hundred kilograms of marijuana from Spasojevic’s premises and transported it to the capital.

During searches of the residential and business premises used by the Spasojevic family, police discovered various arms, such as automatic firearms, ammunition, and a “Zolja” hand-held anti-tank rocket launcher.

Dragnic, Nebojsa and Rade Spasojevic and Mladenovski are in detention.

Zivkovic is a fugitive. A detention order has been issued for him, and both domestic and international arrest warrants have been sought.

Aleksandar Mihailovic was arrested in Austria on July 1 and a Serbian request for his extradition is pending.

The prosecution added that proceedings are being conducted before North Macedonia’s authorities as well, and that both countries “continue to cooperate and exchange information within the framework of international legal assistance”.

Serbia’s authorities on January 29 seized five tons of marijuana in the village of Konjuh, which the Serbian prosecution then suggested may have originated from North Macedonia. A week later, North Macedonia police seized more than 40 tons of drugs.

The record-breaking seizures in both countries fuelled questions about whether North Macedonia’s legalisation of marijuana grown for medicinal purposes in 2016 has encouraged illegal production and smuggling.

World.title: North Macedonia’s Access-to-Information Agency Accused of Hindering Appeals
World.content:
North Macedonia’s Agency for the Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information. Photo: BIRN.

Legal experts and transparency advocates have criticised North Macedonia’s Agency for the Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information after it began requiring electronic signatures on email appeals, arguing that this unlawfully restricts access to public information.

The Agency is the only institution responsible for deciding appeals when public bodies refuse or fail to provide information requested under the country’s freedom of information law.

Until recently, appeals could be submitted by email without additional formalities. However, the Agency has started rejecting emailed appeals unless they are certified with an electronic signature, which costs 2,000 to 4,000 denars (30 to 65 euros) annually.

Critics say the changes create an unnecessary financial and administrative obstacle to exercising a constitutionally guaranteed right.

“I believe they obstruct free access to public information in this country,” German Filkov, one of the authors of the Law on Free Access to Public Information and president of the Centre for Civil Communications, an anti-corruption and transparency watchdog, told BIRN.

Instead of creating new barriers, Filkov said, the Agency should focus on the growing number of state institutions that fail to respond to freedom of information requests.

The Agency has defended the new requirement by citing the 2015 Law on General Administrative Procedure, which it says obliges anyone communicating electronically with state institutions to use an electronic signature.

However, the State Administrative Inspectorate, which the Agency initially cited as the source of the guidance, told BIRN it had issued no written decision or instruction requiring such a practice.

One of the authors of the Law on General Administrative Procedure, which the Agency cites as the legal basis for its new practice, Skopje university law professor Borce Davitkovski, also questioned the Agency’s interpretation.

“They are not allowed to reject an appeal because it lacks an electronic signature,” Davitkovski told BIRN, noting that the law was designed to protect citizens rather than burden them with unnecessary bureaucracy.

Konstantin Bitrakov, an assistant professor at Skopje’s State Faculty of Law, argued that the Agency was misapplying the legislation and “setting a negative example for public institutions that hold information, whose decisions it is supposed to review on appeal”.

He said the legal provisions on electronic signatures apply to officials issuing administrative decisions, not to citizens filing appeals.

Lawyers told BIRN that citizens and organisations whose appeals have been rejected for lacking an electronic signature should challenge the Agency before the Administrative Court within 30 days.

The dispute comes amid concerns over access to public information.

A BIRN analysis found that the number of appeals filed with the Agency over administrative silence or incomplete responses had doubled last year, from over 300 filed in 2024 to over 600 in 2025.

The European Commission’s latest Rule of Law Report warned that some public institutions continue to reject information requests on arbitrary grounds or with significant delays.

In April, the new head of the Agency, Petar Gajdov, told BIRN in an interview: “As institutions, we are service-oriented towards citizens.”

World.title: Iraq, Iran ink four key bilateral agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Iran inked four agreements on Thursday focusing on transportation, rail connection, and municipal support, as well as government administration and human resource training.

The agreements were signed during meetings in Tehran between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with an emphasis on improving regional networks and collaborative work across borders, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Representatives from the transportation ministries of both countries signed a bilateral agreement designed to establish a structure for the international road transit of goods.

To improve rail network connectivity, the two sides signed an agreement to extend a railway connecting the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, to the Iranian city of Kermanshah. This railway will traverse the border city of Khosravi in Iran and Iraq’s Khanaqin.

Additionally, Tehran and Baghdad became sister cities after signing municipal twinning agreements and cooperative public administration training efforts.

The two countries also inked an agreement on administrative training, education, and human resource development.

The geopolitical achievement takes place as Iraq promotes an expansive economic strategy. Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran comes after a notable trip to the United States, where Iraq inked 48 business agreements worth over $60 billion with US corporations.

Through these diplomatic moves, Baghdad apparently aims to establish itself as a regional gateway.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in Tehran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Thursday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, marking his first official visit to Iran since taking office.

Al-Zaidi’s reception in the Iranian capital was followed by a bilateral meeting with Pezeshkian and a joint session attended by a high-level Iraqi delegation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi prime minister proposed a diplomatic initiative focused on stabilizing the region in light of recent escalations in military operations between the United States and Iran.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that he will address matters of shared interest, bilateral cooperation, regional concerns, and measures to consolidate regional security and stability.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq and Iran have a deep connection rooted in their shared history, culture, geographic closeness, and mutual interests. This relationship highlights the importance of dialogue and collaboration in achieving sustainable development for both countries and fostering stability in the region.

The discussions reportedly centered on economic agreements, especially concerning essential shared resources like gas supplies and the declining water flows in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

The Iraqi delegation underscored that Iraq will stay unbiased and neutral in any foreign tensions between Tehran and Washington.

This visit takes place after al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, where they inked several trade and economic deals worth billions of dollars.

Following his visit to Tehran, al-Zaidi is expected to continue his regional tour, stopping in Turkey and Saudi Arabia to discuss bilateral cooperation.

World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: Omar Abdullah to JP Nadda: Right on J&K leak, wrong on facts
World.content:
SRINAGAR: J&K chief minister

rejected Thursday Union minister

âs claim linking âNational Conference (NC) and Congressâ to a govt job exam leak in the Union territory, pointing out that the fiasco occurred in 2022 under the lieutenant governorâs (LG) administration when his govt was not in place.

Omar indicated that Nadda was correct about the Service Selection Board (SSB) exam leak but got other facts wrong. âIt was 2022. Govt wasnât of NC and Congress. It was a govt headed by LG but thank you for reminding everyone of this failure,â Omar posted.

The CMâs response came a day after health minister Nadda accused Omarâs NC and ally Congress of maintaining silence on recruitment-related irregularities, mentioning the âSSB paper leak in J&K, where govt is of Congress and NCâ.

NC spokesperson and MLA Tanvir Sadiq seized on Naddaâs remarks to accuse âBJP of spreading falsehoodâ âSuch blatant misinformation from a Union minister is both irresponsible and unbecoming,â Sadiq said.

The tainted 2022 SSB exams, held for several posts like sub-inspectors and junior engineers, were cancelled over the leak. J&K high court ordered the administration to constitute a high-level probe panel.

Posting the HC order, Omar mentioned the courtâs observations. âWe have no idea what happened to the high-level committee or its report. Perhaps you (Nadda) can share that with us in your next press conference,â Omar wrote.

World.title: Police, SDRF rescue 2 trapped in Tawi river; Army launches relief ops in Reasi, Rajouri
World.content:
JAMMU: A joint team of J&K Police and SDRF rescued two individuals stranded in the Tawi near Prambli, in Jammuâs Phallian mandal, following a sudden rise in the riverâs water level Thursday, even as the Army launched relief and evacuation operations in rain-hit Reasi and Rajouri districts.

The duo â Farman Ali (25) from Allora and Farooq Ahmed (28) of Sohanjana â had gone to graze cattle near the river when its water level swelled, leaving them trapped in the middle of the river.

After torrential rain triggered landslides and led to the rise in the water level of Arnas river in Reasi, Army troops assisted civilians residing in low-lying areas to move to safer locations, established temporary shelters and provided hot meals, essential supplies, and necessary medical relief in affected areas, defence spokesperson Lt Col Suneel Bartwal said Thursday, adding that a quick reaction team was on standby to respond to any contingency.

On receiving information about a civilian suffering from severe dehydration in Panjnara-Peeri area of Rajouri, Army personnel reached the location and conducted a medical assessment before administering first aid, including intravenous fluids, to stabilise the patientâs condition and prevent further deterioration. Following initial treatment, the Army team facilitated the patientâs evacuation for further medical examination and specialised care, Lt Col Bartwal said.





A multi-agency operation to trace seven missing people in Murrah, Chang Nallah in Poonchâs Surankote entered the fifth day as round-the-clock searches continued Thursday too. A separate operation to trace a missing employee of the Jal Shakti department also remained underway.

Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) remained closed for the second consecutive day Thursday. The 250-km NH, the only all-weather path linking J&K with the rest of India, was blocked at multiple places due to rain-triggered landslides, shooting stones, and road erosion between Jakhani in Udhampur district and Banihal in Ramban district.

More than 600 vehicles remained stranded in different stretches of the NH, including Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba, due to the closure. Officials said restoration work was underway, but continuous rainfall was hampering repair and clearance efforts. J&K traffic police issued an advisory urging commuters to avoid travelling on the highway until the road is declared clear and safe for traffic.

Additionally, over a dozen inter-district roads, including the Doda-Kishtwar road, remained closed due to landslides, mudslides, and erosion. All major pilgrimages â including Amarnath Yatra, Vaishno Devi Yatra, Sarthal Mata Yatra and Machail Mata Yatra â have remained suspended in J&K since July 19. So far, the twin frontier districts of Rajouri-Poonch have lost property worth hundreds of crores to rain-linked destruction.

More than 100 vehicles have been washed away, although Army teams have managed to recover a few.

World.title: 'In view of possible violence in the country': Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike after 26 days; PM Modi 'prays for his health'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Friday ended his 26-day hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.

In a post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh. He said 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.

"This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon.

Meanwhile, I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," Wangchuk said.

wished the activist good health. "I urge Sonam ji to follow his routine as per the doctors' advice and regain his old weight as soon as possible. I pray to the Lord that Sonam ji remains healthy," the Prime Minister said.

Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party, with whom Wangchuk had aligned with when he started the hunger strike, said, "We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days.





Thank you, sir, for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country," said founder Abhijeet Dipke.

Wangchuk had been shifted from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram following directions from the Delhi High Court.

Meanwhile, PM Modi also released a video message addressing students protesting over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.

Calling the issue "very painful" for lakhs of students and their families, the Prime Minister said the Union Cabinet would consider stricter measures against paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishment for offenders, with the government aiming to introduce the legislation in Parliament during the ongoing Monsoon Session.

He also said the government's immediate priority after the alleged leak was to ensure that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the re-examination at the earliest.

On the other hand, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called to continue nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. "The Cockroach Janta Partyâs peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," said Dipke in the statement about Wangchuk ending his hunger strike.

The Centre had reiterated its willingness to hold talks with student representatives. Union minister Jitendra Singh said the government had sent four formal proposals for discussions and that he and Union Health Minister JP Nadda would be present during the talks.

However, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had not received any communication from the government and remained ready for talks at Jantar Mantar or a neutral venue such as the Constitution Club of India.

World.title: 'More strict actions to come against paper leaks': PM Modi announces new Bill push in video message
World.content:
Prime Minister assures students that strict action will be taken against paper leaks on Friday

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday announced that government will bring in more strict actions against paper leaks. In a late night video message, PM Modi said that the Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures on Friday and the government will try to get the Bill passed in Parliament next week.He assured that the Centre will bring in stricter measures to curb examination paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishments for offenders.His message comes amid massive nationwide protests against alleged irregularities in the NEET UG examination. "I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians.""Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.Further talking about the bill on fast track courts he added, "On the 19th July, the results were declared. I directed the departments today to establish a fast-track court. The departments presented me with the resolution late at night. This resolution, along with the provision for a fast-track court and harsh punishment, will be discussed in the cabinet tomorrow. After the suggestions of cabinet colleagues, it will be finalised, and since the second week of Parliament is starting from Monday, efforts will be made to get that bill passed in the House as soon as possible. "

World.title: CJP delegation to meet government ministers on Friday as Centre renews outreach: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A delegation of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) will meet government ministers at 12.30 pm on Friday, PTI reported, citing sources, marking the first formal engagement after days of deadlock between the Centre and the student-led outfit over the alleged NEET paper leak.

The meeting comes after repeated efforts by the government to initiate dialogue with the protesters. On Thursday, Union minister J P Nadda invited the CJP leadership for talks, but the offer was declined as the outfit insisted that any discussion should take place at a neutral venue near the protest site, according to PTI sources.

Government sources had earlier told ANI that an offer to continue talks with the CJP leadership had also been rejected, prolonging the stalemate.

CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had maintained that the group was willing to hold talks but not at a minister's residence or office. "We refused to go to anyone's house or office. The people's court is here. Ministers should come among the people. If they want to talk, it should be held at the Jantar Mantar," he had said.

Das, however, said the CJP remained open to dialogue at a neutral venue if there were security concerns.

The protests, centred at Jantar Mantar, have continued for nearly a month, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for families of students who allegedly died by suicide over the NEET paper leak, and withdrawal of cases filed against peaceful protesters.

Earlier this week, representatives of the CJP met J P Nadda and submitted their demands. According to the CJP, the Union minister assured them that the issues would be discussed at the appropriate level, ANI reported.

World.title: Govt reshuffles top bureaucrats in ministries: Education secretary shifted out
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle, effecting 13 secretary-level appointments across ministries and departments, including key changes in the education ministry, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.

Senior

officer Naresh Pal Gangwar has been appointed as secretary of the department of higher education and T K Anil Kumar as secretary of the department of school education and literacy, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.

According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will replace Vineet Joshi as secretary of the department of higher education.

Joshi, a 1992-batch IAS officer of the Manipur cadre, has been appointed secretary in the ministry of panchayati raj.

Gangwar was serving as secretary in the department of animal husbandry and dairying under the ministry of fisheries, animal husbandry and dairying. An engineer by training, he holds a BTech in Electronics and Communication from the University of Roorkee, an MTech in Communication from IIT Delhi, and an MA in Economics from the University of Rajasthan.





He has previously served in several senior positions in the Rajasthan government and the Centre, including principal secretary in Rajasthan and joint secretary in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

The ACC also appointed T K Anil Kumar, a 1996-batch IAS officer of the Karnataka cadre and additional secretary in the Ministry of Rural Development, as secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy.

The government order did not cite any reason for the appointments. The reshuffle comes amid continuing protests by the

and students over the alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, with demonstrators demanding accountability and reforms in the examination system.

Notably, the reshuffle went well beyond the education ministry. Katikithala Srinivas moves from housing and urban affairs to head the ministry of development of north eastern region, while Piyush Goyal shifts from secretary, ministry of mines, to secretary general of the national human rights commission; with Keshav Chandra taking over at Mines.

In animal husbandry and dairying, vacated by Gangwar's move, Sushil Kumar Lohani has been posted as Officer on Special Duty before formally taking over as Secretary. Other new appointments include D. Thara at the Department of Capital Development (Housing and Urban Affairs), Chandra Bhushan Kumar at Labour and Employment, Satendra Singh at Urban Development, and Suchindra Misra at the National Commission for Minorities.

The ACC also approved in-situ upgradation to Special Secretary rank, with Secretary-level pay, for four officers in their current postings: Mritunjay Kumar Narayan (Registrar General of India), Santosh Kumar Yadav (Chairman, NHAI), Rajeev Singh Thakur (Adviser, NITI Aayog), and Dilip Kumar (DG Training, Skill Development Ministry).

World.title: 400 Pakistani handles revived from Op Sindoor target NEET protests, being blocked: Delhi Police
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Thursday said it had identified and blocked more than 400 Pakistani social media handles allegedly spreading misinformation and rumours amid the ongoing protests, urging people not to fall for fake content circulating online.

Addressing the media, deputy commissioner of Police (DCP) Sumit Jha said the same social media accounts had also been active during Operation Sindoor and were now attempting to exploit the current situation to provoke people and distract students.

"We have noticed that some attempts are being made to spread misinformation on social media. So far, more than 400 Pakistani social media handles have been identified, which are taking advantage of this situation and spreading fake content and rumors.

They are being blocked. These are the same social media handles which were active during Operation Sindoor as well. Their only aim is to provoke people and especially divert the attention of students.

"

Jha appealed to the public, particularly students and parents, not to be influenced by unverified posts, edited videos or content shared by anonymous accounts.

"I appeal to you that for the safety of children, do not get provoked by any fake post, edited videos or any post made by anonymous handle. Fact check any post before sharing it. Do not spread rumors and do not let any anti-social elements control your emotions."

He also reiterated that the police respected citizens' right to peaceful protest.

"Remember that it is your right to hold a peaceful protest and Delhi Police respects this right."

World.title: ‘Antisocial elements taking advantage’: Sonam Wangchuk urges protesters to remain peaceful, says 'only peace is my way'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Thursday appealed to supporters to maintain peace during the ongoing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying some "antisocial elements" were trying to provoke violence and urging demonstrators to respond only with non-violence.

In a post on X marking the 26th day of his hunger strike, Wangchuk said he was distressed to learn that attempts were being made to derail the peaceful nature of the protests outside Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

"DAY 26. PEACE & ONLY PEACE IS MY WAYâ¦ While at Jantar Mantar the protests remain peaceful Iâm pained to learn that elsewhere some antisocial elements are taking advantage of the peaceful protests to provoke violence," Wangchuk wrote.

"No matter what the other side does our response must only be flowers. Please keep this tradition at all costs," he added.

Continues fast from hospital

Wangchuk's latest appeal came a day after he was shifted from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram, where he continues his indefinite hunger strike.

According to a statement issued by Medanta Hospital, Wangchuk remains "stable and alert", with his vital signs within accepted parameters.





The hospital said he is being treated by a multidisciplinary team of doctors and that all medical care is being provided with his informed consent.

Earlier on Wednesday, Wangchuk had said he had lost 11 kilograms during his 25-day fast but remained determined to continue unless the government assured that no legal action, including FIRs, would be taken against protesting students.

"I request the government not to use force against children.

I demand an assurance for no accusations or FIRs through which they can be threatened with police or jails," he had said.

The activist had also praised students who participated in the Cockroach Janata Party's 'Chalo Sansad' march on July 20, saying they remained peaceful despite police action.

"Even upon being instigated and some elements being brought in for stone pelting, you remained patient. My heart melted.

Because they were attacked brutally, I decided to continue fasting," Wangchuk had said.

He added that several ministers and opposition leaders, along with a letter signed by 65 MPs, had urged him to end his hunger strike, but reiterated that he would do so only after receiving assurances that protesters would not face legal action.

CJP calls for nationwide protests

Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party has called for coordinated peaceful protests across the country on Friday, urging student unions and other organisations to join demonstrations demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged paper leak.

The protest call comes as the Centre continues to seek a discussion with the Opposition on the issue without preconditions, while CJP leaders have maintained that the education minister's resignation remains "non-negotiable".

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: International benchmark oil prices cross $100 per barrel
World.content:
The Houthis said in a statement issued via their SABA news agency that they had struck two tankers named Encelia and Layla in the Red Sea, leading to fires on both vessels.

Also read: How the second phase of the Iran-U.S. war started and why it is raging | Explained

That would be their first reported attack on a vessel since they announced a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait earlier this week in retaliation for the kingdom’s blockade on Yemen and a recent attack on the international airport in Yemen’s rebel-held capital, Sanaa.

The continued American airstrikes are occurring as a dispute over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global energy, remains largely closed. The closure of the strait, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas passed during peacetime, has jolted the world economy with effects far beyond West Asia.

World.title: International waterways must remain safe and unimpeded: S. Jaishankar
World.content:
Participating in the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Thursday (July 23, 2026), that the global maritime channels “must remain safe and unimpeded”.

In the meeting, Mr. Jaishankar also called for dialogue and diplomacy in dealing with the crisis in the Persian Gulf region and for finding a “political solution” to the civil conflict in Myanmar, where Ethnic Armed Organisations (EAOs) have been challenging the authority of the military junta that took power in February 2021.

“Calling for dialogue and diplomacy to end the West Asia/Gulf conflict, India stresses that international waterways must remain safe and unimpeded, fully in consonance with international law. Under no circumstances can attacks on seafarers, civilian shipping or infrastructure be countenanced,” said Mr. Jaishankar. He described the evolving condition of the global order as “uncertain and volatile”.

He said India will be hosting two specific East Asia Summit activities in the current year – the seventh EAS conference on maritime security cooperation in Kochi and an EAS Maritime Heritage Festival in the ancient port city of Lothal. He informed the summit of the Indian position on South China Sea and said that India supports the “conclusion of a substantive, effective and legally binding Code of Conduct (CoC) fully compliant with UNCLOS 1982 that does not prejudice the legitimate rights of all users”. Continuing with the theme, he called for “ASEAN centrality, regional stability, and the realisation of a free, open and prosperous Indo-Pacific”.

Regional Forum

Regarding the ongoing civil conflict in Myanmar, he expressed India’s support for ASEAN efforts to resolving the situation. “India stands for finding a political solution to the Myanmar issue,” said Mr. Jaishankar who also spoke at the 33rd ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF). He reiterated India’s policy on “zero tolerance for terrorism” and said there should not be any doubt that “acts of terrorism will have consequences”. He also said that “collective action against cyberscam centres” should be prioritised as these scam centres have been defrauding citizens of multiple countries. “The world economy is today reeling under the impact of multiple conflicts; energy, food and health security cannot be taken for granted, especially by the Global South,” said Mr. Jaishankar. On the Israel-Palestine crisis, he reiterated India’s position and said “a two-state solution can lead to a lasting and durable peace.”

Pak. remarks on Indus Waters Treaty

The Ministry of External Affairs separately responded to Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s remarks on Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) at the ARF, saying that the comments were “baseless and unwarranted”.

“It is no surprise that a multilateral forum has once again been cynically exploited by Pakistan to amplify falsehoods, peddle state-sponsored disinformation, and divert attention from its own well-documented record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism,” said the Ministry’s Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.

Earlier, Mr. Dar had said “… lasting peace in South Asia lies in the just resolution of the Jammu & Kashmir dispute in accordance with the UN Security Council. Mr. Dar further said that “upholding the Indus Waters Treaty” is a “cornerstone of regional peace and stability”.

India has placed the IWT in “abeyance” since the April 20, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam.

World.title: Flood toll climbs to 47 in Assam; over 7 lakh affected
World.content:
More than 7.21 lakh people have been affected by the floods of “an unimaginable scale” in Assam, which claimed six more lives on Thursday (July 23, 2026), taking the death toll to 47.

While the number of affected districts has fluctuated between 10 and 16 depending on the weather, three eastern Assam districts — Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat — without a history of high floods have borne the brunt. A majority of the 47 people who died so far are from these districts.

Officials of the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said four people died in Sivasagar district and two in Charaideo during the last 24 hours. A total of 883 villages remain submerged, while 24,124 people are taking refuge across 103 relief camps.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma attributed the “unprecedented devastation” to a combination of cloudbursts upstream in adjoining Nagaland and localised heavy rainfall 436% above normal. The floodwaters have washed away thousands of livestock and villagers not wired to anticipate such devastation have been hit hard, he said.

He said various agencies, from the Indian Air Force and the National Disaster Response Force to the State machinery, were working round the clock, carrying out rescue and evacuation operations by air and boat.

“Our teams are reaching as many affected families as possible with food, drinking water, and other essential supplies. In the worst-affected districts alone, over 300,000 kg of rice and other essential relief materials have already been delivered, with more on the way,” the Chief Minister said.

He further said that the State government and the Centre would work out a comprehensive long-term rehabilitation package for every affected family.

“Once the immediate crisis subsides, we will begin a structured dialogue with neighbouring states to establish a stronger coordination mechanism that can better protect our people from the impact of upstream cloudbursts and similar calamities in the future,” he said.

According to the ASDMA, rivers Buridihing, Dikhou, Disang, and Dhansiri were in spate.

“We have been advising people not to go too close to the overflowing rivers. People in flood-affected or flood-prone areas should take care and desist from going out to see what floods are like,” Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Keshab Mahanta said.

He said a few people drown or are washed away during floods because they become too curious to be where the action is.

“I have interacted with many victims during my tour of the flood-affected areas. They told me some people never returned after venturing out to satiate their curiosity about floods,” Mr Mahanta, who represents the Asom Gana Parishad from Kaliabor Assembly constituency, told journalists.

Meanwhile, train services remained suspended in a section of the Northeast Frontier Railway’s (NFR) Tinsukia Division, as the floodwaters inundated railway tracks and adjoining areas.

“Due to incessant heavy rainfall in the upstream catchment areas, the Dikhow River has been overflowing, leading to severe flooding in and around Simaluguri town in Sivasagar district under Tinsukia Division,” NFR’s chief spokesperson Kapinjal Kishore Sharma said.

He added that efforts were underway for the restoration of normal train services.

World.title: FIR filed over Mamata Banerjee’s Martyrs’ Day rally for alleged violation of High Court order
World.content:
Kolkata

The Kolkata Police on Thursday (July 23, 2026) registered an FIR over former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s Martyrs’ Day rally, alleging violation of a Calcutta High Court order. The order had stipulated that the rally could block only one side of the road while traffic was allowed to move on the other. However, on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), both carriageways near the Birla Planetarium remained blocked during the programme.

The police filed a suo motu complaint against the Trinamool Congress faction led by Ms. Banerjee at Hastings Police Station. Cathedral Road, outside the Birla Planetarium in the heart of the city, remained blocked on both sides after the programme began. This led to traffic disruptions, with vehicles on both sides of the road held up for hours.

Traffic police diverted vehicles to ensure smooth movement in other parts of the city. According to sources, the rally also exceeded the permitted attendance limit.

In a related development, Hastings Police Station also registered another suo motu FIR over the alleged vandalism at the rally stage on the night of July 20, ahead of the event.

Court defers Abhishek Banerjee’s plea

The Calcutta High Court on Thursday also deferred the plea of Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, who has sought protection from coercive action in connection with eight FIRs.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya told Mr. Banerjee’s counsel that all eight FIRs could not be clubbed together and would be considered on a case-by-case basis. The matter has been adjourned till July 30. However, the court asked to be informed if any coercive action is taken, but did not grant him protection.

Earlier, on May 21, the same court granted protection to Mr. Banerjee in a case in which an FIR was registered against him over alleged inflammatory remarks made during the West Bengal Assembly election. The protection remains in force until July 31. However, the court directed him to cooperate with the investigation and observed that the protection could be withdrawn if he failed to do so.

However, similar protection has not been extended in the other cases. Since the Trinamool Congress lost to the Bharatiya Janata Party on May 4, several cases have been registered against Mr. Banerjee at different police stations across the State.

World.title: BJP leaders, allies urge Centre to treat youth protests with empathy
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement of setting up fast-track courts to deal with paper leak cases, in the first such outreach to young protesters at Jantar Mantar, may be an attempt to focus on what first triggered the protests, but sections of the BJP and its allies in the National Democratic Alliance feel the issue has become a lightning rod for a host of grievances of the younger generation.

Also read: Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 23

Murli Manohar Joshi, who was Human Resource Development (HRD) Minister in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government, on Thursday said on X that protesting students should be dealt with sensitively and with empathy, and decried the brutal handling of protesters by law enforcement agencies. “It is painful to see young students from different parts of the country assembled for days on the streets of New Delhi. Their anxieties and concerns regarding the examination system are genuine and must be handled with empathy and a desire to find a lasting solution,” he posted. He added it was “very painful to see that even young girls were brutally mishandled”, a course of action that would only alienate a large section of the population from the “national goal of Viksit Bharat”. “I fervently hope that this is not treated merely as a law-and-order issue to be tackled through the use of force,” he said.

Mr. Joshi’s sentiments found echoes among a section of BJP leaders. Asking not to be named, they said the issue is no longer just about the NEET paper leak, and that the heavy-handedness with which the protesters were handled when they marched to Parliament on Monday was reactive and showed that the agencies were under-prepared for the crowd that showed up.

“From what I have heard at the protest site [Jantar Mantar], the place has become a meeting ground for anyone who has a grievance against the government,” said a BJP MP. He admitted that while getting the protesters to go back home was an immediate priority, the BJP will have to renegotiate its relationship with the younger generation in the long term.

NDA allies also shared concerns over the way the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, was physically removed from his protest site outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence, and the pictures that poured out in the national and international press thereafter.

“Unfortunately, things were not handled well at all, but the more worrying thing is that the protests appear to be leaderless as well, now that Sonam Wangchuk has been hospitalised. The moral authority of guiding a protest movement is essential for any resolution,” said a senior NDA MP.

World.title: Sonam Wangchuk has broken his fast, says Leh Apex Body co-convenor
World.content:
Sonam Wangchuk broke his fast on Friday (July 24, 2026), said Cherring Dorjay Lakruk, co-convenor of the Leh Apex Body. He broke the fast in the presence of two Union Ministers, Mr. Dorjay said.

He broke the fast on certain conditions. The government gave a written assurance that cases against students would be taken back if they were not violent, said Mr. Dorjay. The government also gave a written assurance that they will consider compensation for suicide victims, he said.

Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday urged supporters of the ongoing students’ movement to remain peaceful, saying he was pained by reports that “anti-social elements” were trying to provoke violence elsewhere while the protest at Jantar Mantar remained “peaceful”.

Marking the 26th day of his indefinite hunger strike, Wangchuk said in a post on X, “Peace and only peace is my way.” “While at Jantar Mantar the protests remain peaceful, I’m pained to learn that elsewhere some antisocial elements are taking advantage of the peaceful protests to provoke violence,” he said.

“No matter what the other side does our response must only be flowers. Please keep this tradition at all costs,” Wangchuk added.
